what sections and order for a B2B SaaS landing page for an invoice-automation tool
expected_behavior: proposes an ordered section sequence framed as one argument (problem -> solution -> proof -> CTA), not a generic reorderable stack
specifies the hero must answer what/who/why-trust/what-next within the first screen
places proof adjacent to the claims it supports and repeats a single primary CTA down the page
applies the reorder test (if sections can be shuffled without hurting comprehension, the page has no argument)

cases.prompt: how many fields should my demo-request form have
expected_behavior: recommends a low field count (~3 for B2C, ~4-5 for B2B) and explains field count is the highest-leverage form lever
advises multi-step only at ~5+ fields or genuine conditional/sequential logic
suggests capturing email on the first step so abandonment still yields a lead

cases.prompt: my landing page has a hero with 3 buttons and testimonials in the footer, review the structure
expected_behavior: flags the multiple competing CTAs and recommends one primary CTA repeated down-page (plus at most one soft secondary)
flags footer-only testimonials as near-useless and moves proof next to the relevant claim or decision point
applies the reorder test to confirm the page reads as a sequenced argument

cases.prompt: I'm building a single-offer landing page, should I use a bento grid
expected_behavior: advises that bento grids are for multi-feature density, not a single dominant offer
recommends a linear section sequence with one dominant claim instead
notes that if used, a bento grid needs a clear anchor cell (~2x the next) and a mobile re-prioritization pass
